title: A Ledger for the Witness
premise: When the coffin of Alderfen's founder, Edmund Vasse, is exhumed for a tercentenary ceremony and found empty, true-crime podcaster Beatrix Amberdale is summoned by a dying archivist who leaves them a ledger of names — including Beatrix's own, written in ink that predates their birth. The ledger reveals that every generation, one 'witness' is chosen to carry the town's founding secret: that Edmund never died here at all, and someone has been buried in his name ever since. As the anniversary dinner approaches, Beatrix discovers they were selected as this generation's witness as a child, their memory of it surgically erased by the very family who raised them. In the crypt beneath the town hall, Beatrix finds the living, ancient Edmund — kept alive by the town's inheritance ritual — and must choose between exposing the truth and becoming the next keeper. They broadcast everything live during the anniversary toast, closing the case at last, but the final entry in the ledger is now written in their own hand.
about_author: Astrid Galloway spent a decade transcribing coroner's inquests in coastal market towns before turning to fiction, and her prose carries the cadence of sworn testimony. She writes from a converted tithe barn, where she keeps an unopened ledger she claims was left on her doorstep with no return address.

chapters.title: The Weight of Good Oak
chapters.summary: Beatrix Amberdale, mid-recording of their podcast's finale episode, witnesses the exhumation of founder Edmund Vasse and the discovery of an empty coffin lined with fresh moss. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: professional thrill curdling into unease when the gravedigger whispers that the coffin has been 'light' for years.

chapters.title: A Dying Hand, A Steady Line
chapters.summary: The town archivist, Maren Quill, summons Beatrix to her deathbed and presses a leather ledger into their hands — its pages list one name per generation, and the newest entry reads 'B. Amberdale' in ink two decades old. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity; Beatrix realizes they've been chosen before they ever chose.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore It Was Closed
chapters.summary: Beatrix investigates the only death officially tied to Vasse: his daughter Cordelia's drowning in 1897, ruled accidental and sealed by court order. Interviews with elderly townsfolk reveal identical, rehearsed phrasing across generations. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the podcaster's confidence cracks as they hear their own childhood phrases repeated back to them.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers Me
chapters.summary: Beatrix returns to the Amberdale family home and finds a child's drawing of the crypt beneath the town hall — signed with their own name, aged six. Their aunt Halcyon admits Beatrix was taken below once, and came back 'wrong.' POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal; memory becomes an unreliable inheritance.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Ledger
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing the ledger with parish records, Beatrix learns Cordelia Vasse wrote the first entries before her 'drowning' — and that each witness since has died within a year of passing the book on. POV: alternating Beatrix and interpolated ledger entries. Emotional beat: mounting horror as pattern replaces coincidence.

chapters.title: Salt in the Foundation Stones
chapters.summary: Days before the anniversary dinner, someone ransacks Maren's archive and the ledger goes missing; Beatrix suspects Halcyon, who has begun quietly selling off family land. A threatening note arrives: 'Witnesses watch. Keepers keep.' POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: isolation — the town closes ranks around its secret.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Toast
chapters.summary: At the tercentenary dinner, Beatrix publicly announces they will open the crypt at midnight, forcing the town's elders to choose between stopping them and revealing themselves. Halcyon, unexpectedly, hands Beatrix the stolen ledger back. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: defiance sharpened by the realization that Halcyon wants the secret ended too.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: In the crypt, Beatrix finds not bones but a man — Edmund Vasse himself, sustained for three centuries by the ritual the ledger describes, fed by each generation's witness. He recognizes Beatrix instantly: 'You screamed so beautifully, little one.' POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: terror giving way to terrible compassion for a man who cannot die and cannot be remembered.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Keeper
chapters.summary: Edmund offers Beatrix the succession: take the ledger, take the burden, let the town stay whole — or burn the ledger and end him, unraveling the inheritance that built Alderfen. Halcyon arrives and confesses she erased Beatrix's memory to spare them this exact moment. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the climax of identity — choosing what to inherit versus what to become.

chapters.title: Read Aloud, Then Closed
chapters.summary: During the final toast, Beatrix livestreams the ledger's full contents and Edmund's confession, then burns the book as he dissolves into the crypt dust that founded the town. The case closes; the podcast ends. Weeks later, a new ledger appears on Beatrix's doorstep, first page blank except for their own handwriting already drying. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — some inheritances survive even their destruction.
